mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention member states: notarize a certified copy, then obtain an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT). For non-member states: do not use an Apostille; after MFAT authentication of the underlying signature/certificate, complete consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate in New Zealand. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention member states: notarize a certified copy, then obtain an Apostille from MFAT. For non-member states: no Apostille; after MFAT authentication, follow consular legalization at the destination foreign mission in New Zealand. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company board of directors and company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private instrument: execute in accordance with the company constitution, certify as true by an authorized officer, notarize before a New Zealand Notary Public, and then, for member states, obtain an MFAT Apostille. For non-member states, after notarization proceed directly to consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate in New Zealand; no Apostille is issued or used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company shareholders and directors as adopted on incorporation; registered copy at the NZ Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention member states: obtain a certified registered copy from the Companies Office, notarize if required, and then obtain an MFAT Apostille. For non-member states: use the parallel consular legalization route only, beginning with MFAT authentication and ending at the destination consulate in New Zealand; Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand registered bank (major trading bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private bank document: issued on bank letterhead, signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized by a New Zealand Notary Public; for Apostille Convention member states, obtain an MFAT Apostille; for non-member states, after notarization and without an Apostille, submit to the destination embassy or consulate in New Zealand for consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All customers, directors, shareholders, signatories, beneficiaries and any beneficial owner holding 25% or more must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand autonomous sanctions lists maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, and, as an enhanced best practice, the OFAC SDN List. Politically Exposed Persons, their close associates and family members are subject to enhanced due diligence with written risk assessment, source of wealth verification, and senior management approval. Any adverse match requires immediate refusal of transaction and, where legally required, submission of a suspicious transaction report to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Online and NZBN Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in English, te reo Maori, or another language provided they are rendered in Latin-script characters. Phonetic transliteration into English must be supplied where the name uses non-Latin script or unusual spelling to permit screening. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) distinctive ordinary identifier; (2) descriptive business qualifier; (3) mandatory legal form indicator, namely Limited or Ltd; and (4) special approval marker where a regulated word such as Bank or Trust is used, requiring prior ministerial or authority consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office refuses a prospective name, request a written statement of reasons from the Business Registration Support team. Within 20 working days file a formal review application to the Registrar of Companies under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993, attaching evidence of prior use, trade mark registration, or written consent from any affected competent authority. If review is unsuccessful, the applicant may commence judicial review proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand. No materially identical name may be registered while an appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used solely as a New Zealand physical address for service of process, provided a registered agent accepts documents at that street address; however, a commercial mailbox or virtual office alone is not permitted as the principal place of business for this specialty tea salon lounge. Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks require an actual trading location to approve GST registration and business account opening, and the local municipal council requires a physical food and beverage premises for licensing, food safety inspection and public health approval; therefore only a fully leased and operational physical tea salon satisfies commercial substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) trading premises visible with exterior signage; (ii) on-site tea equipment, inventory and ceremonial service furniture; (iii) point-of-sale systems and contemporaneous sales records; (iv) employees or owner physically present during trading hours; (v) lease, food business registration and local council licences available for inspection. Quantified risk: unannounced inspections by local council health and building authorities and by Inland Revenue are medium-high for an in-scope food beverage premises, estimated at 35% probability in the first 12 months of operation and approximately 15% per year thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), including sections 5, 10, 12, 13, 154, 161 and Schedule 1; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2006; Financial Reporting Act 2013
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Register online form authenticated via RealMe)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Companies Act 1993; no minimum issued or paid-up share capital is required, and no escrow or blocked bank account is mandated. The subscribers may fix an unlimited or nominal share capital structure and allot shares for a stated cash consideration as a matter of corporate credit policy.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a properly convened and constituted meeting of the board of directors of [Company Name], a limited company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993, held on [Date] at [Registered Office], at which a quorum was present, the following resolutions were considered and duly passed: 1. Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED that the initial issue of shares to the subscribers be and is hereby ratified and approved, and that the consideration subscription of NZ$[Amount] for the ordinary shares shall be paid in cash in full on allotment into the company's designated bank account. The directors are authorized to record allotments in the share register, issue share certificates, and undertake any filings required by the Companies Office. 2. Adoption of Constitution and Registered Office. RESOLVED that the constitution submitted with the application for registration be adopted as the company's constitution and that the registered office and address for service shall be maintained at [New Zealand Address]. The board is authorized to notify the New Zealand Companies Office of any subsequently changed address and to appoint and receive service through an approved person. 3. Banking Authority. RESOLVED that the company shall maintain one or more bank accounts with a licensed New Zealand bank, and that the following officers be appointed as authorized signatories [Officer A], [Officer B], and [Officer C] and that all cheques and electronic funds transfers require the signature of at least two officers acting jointly, or such other mandate as the board may set in a banking resolution. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments and Compliance. RESOLVED that [Director A] be appointed statutory director and that [Director B] be appointed as responsible officer for compliance and risk. Each appointee accepts office under the Companies Act 1993. The executive is expressly authorized to apply for an IRD number, GST registration, and all local food, building, and fire licensing approvals necessary for the tea salon business. 5. Ratification of Formation Acts. RESOLVED that all actions undertaken by the persons named as incorporators in the registration application be hereby ratified in all respects, and that the chairperson and secretary be authorized to sign all consents, statutory declarations and supplementary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Filing, Company Name and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) - Companies Register, online via RealMe login service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register RealMe service and initiate the Register a Company application. Enter the proposed company name and check availability through the registry search. Identify the first director or directors, shareholders, and the authorised person for service, confirm that the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand, and upload or draft the constitution. Each subscriber and director must complete a separate consent declaration electronically; if submitting on paper, wet-ink signatures must be witnessed by an appropriately authorised person or a Justice of the Peace. Pay the stated fee using the secure payment gateway. The application is automatically considered upon submission and routed to the Companies Office for verification under the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Company name approval or reservation confirmation
Constitution (optional but recommended)
Director consent forms required by Companies Act 1993
Shareholder and contributor details with share allocation schedule
Address for service in New Zealand
RealMe identity verification for each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office raises a query, notice of proposed refusal, or registration suspension, respond through the Companies Register portal within 10 working days with corrected information, reconcile name or document objections, and pay any required resubmission fee. If refusal persists, refile a fresh application with a new name or seek judicial review under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and Tax Compliance Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - myIR business portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After company incorporation, await the automatic transmission of company details to the Inland Revenue or create a myIR account for the company using the Companies Office reference. Apply for an IRD number for the company if not auto-issued. Register for GST if the annual turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period, and consider voluntary GST registration from inception if the tea salon intends to claim input credits. Register for PAYE if employees will be hired, and for fringe benefit tax if a vehicle or fringe benefits are provided. Confirm the company address for correspondence and set up account authority for any tax agent or financial controller.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate or Companies Office extract
Directors' IRD numbers and identity documents
Bank account details and postal address
Projected annual income and GST turnover declaration
Legal entity structure confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is queried or placed on hold, submit supplementary materials through myIR secure message within 10 working days, correct any non-resident director or shareholder declarations, and request a review of penalties or interest if delay is administrative. Unresolved income tax disputes may be escalated through the Taxation Review Authority after an internal reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Registration and Premises Food Safety Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries - New Zealand Food Safety and the local territorial authority (city or district council) environmental health office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the specialty tea salon as a food business under the Food Act 2014 by selecting the applicable food service category. Prepare a Food Control Plan based on the Ministry template covering loose-leaf tea procurement, storage, water quality, brewing and serving hygiene, waste disposal, and cleaning schedules. Consult the local council environmental health officer on zoning, trade waste consent, and the location of hand-washing and sanitation facilities. Submit the Food Control Plan, premises floor plans, and operational records schedule to the council or an approved verifier. A pre-opening inspection may be scheduled, after which the registration certificate and any annual renewal conditions are issued.
required_dossiers: Completed Food Act 2014 registration application
Food Control Plan or National Programme template
Floor plan of the premises showing kitchen, service and sanitary areas
Public liability insurance certificate
Trade waste discharge consent or council drainage permit
Staff food safety training records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the council returns the application for incompleteness, cure the stated deficiencies within 10 working days and resubmit. If the inspection reveals non-compliance, implement a corrective action plan with deadlines and obtain a follow-up inspection. If registration is declined, appeal to the District Court or apply for temporary registration while completing remedial works.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Building Code Compliance, Civil Defence Fire Safety and Occupancy Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority building consent authority and Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire protection unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the premises have an existing occupancy approval or obtain a new building consent for any change of use, seating layout, structural alterations, or commercial kitchen ventilation. Engage a licensed building practitioner to certify fire separation, egress paths, exit widths, smoke detection, emergency lighting, and public access compliance under the Building Act 2004 and New Zealand Building Code. Upon completion, obtain a code compliance certificate. Thereafter, maintain an annual building warrant of fitness listing inspections by independent inspectors. Consult FENZ for the fire evacuation scheme and secure service connections for fire alarms and extinguishers before commencing trade.
required_dossiers: Building consent application and approved plans
Licensed building practitioner certificates and producer statements
Construction and durability records
Fire evacuation scheme application to FENZ
Building warrant of fitness inspection records
Certificate of confirmation and operational readiness checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If building consent is refused, amend the plans to satisfy the NZBC clauses and resubmit. If FENZ issues a notice of non-compliance, rectify the listed fire hazards, obtain a final inspection, and maintain a record of the certificate. For historical unauthorised work, apply for a certificate of acceptance where legally permitted to regularise the building before regulatory action matures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Food Safety (Ministry for Primary Industries) and the local territorial authority environmental health, building compliance and civil defence licensing desk
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Control Plan Registration under the Food Act 2014 (premises registration for beverage service)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable for a service-sector tea salon; if resource consent is triggered, the local regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991, with the New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority for nationally significant proposals
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Resource Management Act 1991. A specialty tea service in an existing commercial zone is generally a permitted activity; if a resource consent application is required, an Assessment of Environmental Effects at Category 1 minor level is submitted to the local council.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharge. Wastewater from tea preparation and cleaning must align with municipal trade waste limits: pH 6.0 to 10.0, temperature not exceeding 38 degrees Celsius, biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 300 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, and oils or greases not exceeding 100 mg/L. Ventilation exhaust must comply with NZ Building Code G4 Ventilation with no visible smoke or odour beyond the site boundary. No volatile organic compound solvent use is mandatory for a tea salon; any limited cleaning chemicals must be stored safely and disposed of as non-hazardous waste when below hazardous substance thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) must approve the building fire evacuation scheme where occupant load exceeds 100 persons. The Building Act 2004 requires a Building Warrant of Fitness and annual inspections of fire alarms, extinguishers and exit signage. WorkSafe New Zealand clearance is required for workplace safety, first aid readiness, electrical safety and emergency procedures. Structural load approval, licensed building practitioner certification, and an occupancy certificate must be in place before public service. A verified fire extinguisher, smoke detection, emergency lighting and clear egress pathway record must remain accessible to inspectors at all times.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (Inland Revenue) via the myIR online portal (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir); for export and customs clearance, co-administration by the New Zealand Customs Service using the Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Companies Act 1993, a New Zealand incorporated NZ_LTD obtains its IRD number via the Companies Office registration process, which shares the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and incorporation details with Inland Revenue, after which the Commissioner issues the IRD number. For a foreign non-resident company not incorporated in New Zealand, the entity must first determine whether it is carrying on a taxable activity or has a New Zealand permanent establishment; if so, it must apply on myIR through the Commissioner's prescribed electronic application for a non-resident company IRD number. The application must include: (i) the certificate of incorporation or equivalent foreign corporate registration deed, (ii) constitutional documents or articles of association, (iii) a board resolution appointing a New Zealand agent, branch manager or tax representative where applicable, (iv) certified passport and tax residence declarations for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, (v) a New Zealand business address and bank account mandate, and (vi) evidence of the parent company or shareholder register. Once verified, Inland Revenue issues the IRD number and the entity is placed on the income tax register. For GST, the entity must separately apply for GST registration on myIR under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 if the taxable turnover threshold is met or if voluntary registration is needed for refunds or zero-rating; non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand residents use the simplified non-resident GST registration channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in respect of check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; New Zealand does not have a check-the-box regime. A qualifying close company may elect look-through company (LTC) treatment under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 if all ownership and eligibility tests are satisfied, causing tax transparency for New Zealand-resident owners; hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and non-elective under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including certain non-resident remote services supplied to New Zealand residents; registration is mandatory once the historical or prospective 12-month turnover exceeds the threshold, and voluntary registration is available where the Commissioner is satisfied that the entity carries on a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory invoice stamping, or anti-fraud digital stamp regime exists in New Zealand. GST returns must be filed electronically through myIR. Standard GST invoices must satisfy section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 by showing the supplier name and GST number, invoice date, description, consideration and GST amount. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and is transmitted over the New Zealand Peppol network; there is no mandatory API-based fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when a registered person supplies goods and the goods are physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply. Services are zero-rated under section 11A when supplied to a non-resident recipient outside New Zealand, provided the services are not directly in connection with land in New Zealand, are not physically performed in New Zealand, and the recipient is outside New Zealand at the time of supply. For the specialty tea salon and lounge, on-site retail food and beverage supply is standard-rated at 15% GST; export sales of loose-leaf tea, ceramics and tea ware can be zero-rated as goods if physical export and all statutory evidence are completed within the 28-day rule. There is no separate tourist GST refund administration; rather, suppliers may zero-rate goods that are exported as accompanied baggage only when the prescribed export evidence is obtained and retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export declaration or export entry lodged electronically with the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing dispatch from New Zealand and destination abroad
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the exported tea, ceramics or goods and their value
Bank credit advice, SWIFT MT103, or foreign exchange receipt showing the export proceeds received in the New Zealand bank account (the functional equivalent of an inward remittance certificate)
Proof of non-resident status of the recipient for any zero-rated service supply, including the customer's name, overseas address and tax residency declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may retrospectively assess output GST at 15% on any supply previously zero-rated if the supporting export and proceeds evidence is not maintained, with the general four-year reassessment period under the Tax Administration Act 1994, and no time limit where there is fraud or evasion. Shortfall penalties under Part 7 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at 20% for failure to take reasonable care or an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion; use-of-money interest is also charged from the original due date. Knowingly false or fraudulent export zero-rating claims can give rise to criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994, and directors or responsible officers may be held personally liable where the false GST return was knowingly caused or permitted. To sustain export zero-rating, the complete customs declaration bundle, transport documentation and foreign exchange credit evidence must therefore remain available to Inland Revenue for audit inspection, with the business policy requiring all proceeds to be reconciled within 180 days of export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) under the delegated foreign exchange administration framework of the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations 1977, administered jointly with the New Zealand Treasury
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised and freely floating foreign exchange regime. There are no exchange controls, no mandatory conversion requirements, and no restrictions on current account payments for trade in goods and services, interest, dividends, royalties, or capital account movements such as direct investment, portfolio investment, loans, and repatriation of share capital. The New Zealand dollar is fully convertible on both the current and capital accounts. No permission from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand is required for cross-border transfers, and no prior approval is needed for foreign investors to establish or fund a limited liability company, except for transactions involving sensitive land, significant business assets, or fishing quota under the Overseas Investment Act 2005. Profit remittances by a non-resident shareholder are tax-deductible if subject to non-resident withholding tax and are freely transferable without surrender requirements. Exporters are not required to surrender export receipts, and there is no FX rationing, no multiple exchange rate regime, and no settlement restriction on converting NZD back to home currency. The practical impediment is not regulation but standard bank de-risking due to AML/CFT compliance; therefore documentary evidence of source-of-funds and beneficial ownership must be robust. Overall, convertibility is high and the external accounts are fully open, allowing a specialty tea salon to move capital and operational funds in and out of the country without central bank repurchase or surrender hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender rule in New Zealand. Exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in offshore or onshore accounts, may freely convert proceeds to NZD, or may use them directly for third-party trade settlement, provided the underlying transactions are accurately declared to Customs New Zealand and supported by commercial invoices for AML and Goods and Services Tax (GST) purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are legally constrained in New Zealand because deposit-taking and issuing of demand liabilities require registration as a bank under the Prudential Regulation Framework of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. A general-purpose EMI license comparable to the UK or Singapore model does not exist. Offshore EMIs may only act as payment facilitators or prepaid instrument providers if they partner with a licensed New Zealand bank, but they cannot independently hold corporate treasury balances, provide full settlement accounts, or issue overdraft facilities. Their practical viability is Low for primary receipt of share capital and for critical clearing rails, but Medium as an auxiliary payment gateway for e-commerce orders if the underlying cash settlement is held at a tier-1 local bank. For this treasury blueprint, the specialty tea salon must open a primary corporate operating account at a locally incorporated bank and may use EMIs only for low-value card processing or merchant aggregator services, never for capital escrow, supplier settlement, or FX conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not generally mandatory for New Zealand domestic corporate account opening because banks accept remote verification under the AML/CFT Act 2009 using certified copies of identity documents, digital identity verification, and supervised video interviews. However, for a newly incorporated company with 100% non-resident ownership and a non-resident director or signatory, most tier-1 banks will require either an in-branch interview for the company director and all signatories, or a remote interview with a notarially certified passport and proof of residential address countersigned by a consular officer or an approved notary. Some banks will permit remote opening if a New Zealand-registered director or a local Company Office service provider acts as a compliance contact, but this is at the discretion of the bank's Financial Crime Risk team. A statutory director cannot appoint a proxy without also providing an irrevocable power of attorney and a full source-of-wealth declaration, because the bank's mandatory customer due diligence measures treat the beneficial owner as the principal account holder for risk rating purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with high-risk jurisdiction exposure or opaque corporate chain in the shareholding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised corporate registry extracts for every entity in the ownership chain up to the ultimate individual owner; audited financial statements or sworn asset statements; bank reference letters from a regulated foreign bank; explanation of the commercial purpose for each intermediate company; and a certified copy of each shareholder's passport plus proof of residential address from an independent public utility, tax bill, or government-issued credential dated within the last three months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial share capital deposit into the capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of personal or corporate bank statements covering the exact funding wire; executed sale and purchase agreement if funds originate from disposal of property or business; employment contract or dividend minutes if funds arise from salary or declared profits; stamped board resolution authorising the capital injection; and a notarised letter of undertaking confirming that all funds are beneficially owned by the named contributors and do not derive from third-party financing, loans, or illicit activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Same-day or back-to-back transactions between the NZ company, related foreign entities, and the tea supply chain before any substantive operating history is established
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial supply agreements with packaging, tea processor, and logistics suppliers; pro-forma invoices and shipping documents such as bills of lading and air waybills; a projected cash flow model explaining the business cycle of 60- to 120-day inventory holding; confirmation from the chartered accountant that transactions are aligned with the arm's-length pricing of the Specialty Tea Salon; and copies of all related-party loan or service agreements to demonstrate economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors or signatories are tax residents of a FATF grey-listed or monitored jurisdiction, creating a precautionary freeze risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residency certificate issued by the foreign tax authority; evidence of economic substance and physical business premises in New Zealand, such as an executed office lease, payroll records, or independent accountant confirmation; an outline of all expected funding channels and repayment corridors; and for any director residing in a grey-listed jurisdiction, a prohibition advisory memo from the NZ regulator and a commitment to route all NZD inflows and outflows exclusively through the NZ tier-1 bank to ensure traceability.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital should be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's personal or corporate bank account to the company's NZD capital escrow account at an RBNZ-registered commercial bank. The wire must include the ISO 20022 purpose code or a narrative expressly identifying the transfer as 'share subscription consideration', 'equity contribution', or 'loan to subsidiary', along with the New Zealand Companies Register company number. For values exceeding NZD 50,000, banks require a completed Source of Funds and Source of Wealth declaration. If the capital originates from China, Hong Kong, or other jurisdictions with FX reporting systems, the remitter must confirm the local bank registration and purpose code so that the funds are not mischaracterised as trade payment. After receipt, the bank may hold the capital in escrow until the company issues share certificates and files the shareholder register with the Companies Office. A New Zealand chartered accountant may issue a capital confirmation report supported by real-time bank statements, the board resolution, and correspondent bank MT103 trail. For loans from shareholders, the loan agreement must be notarised and the interest rate should be arm's length to avoid thin capitalisation and withholding tax on royalties or interest. Any physical cash injection is prohibited under AML/CFT.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for specialty tea purchases, custom ceramic ware, packaging, and logistics services should be executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for high-value transactions where the supplier requires direct bank-to-bank credit. For tea imports from origin markets with established trade relationships, an irrevocable at-sight documentary letter of credit (L/C) with a confirmed correspondent bank provides security to the seller and an audit trail for clearing. For repeat medium-volume shipments, documentary collections (CAD or D/P) may reduce transaction costs but provide weaker working capital protection; therefore they are acceptable only for trusted counterparties with no prior discrepancy history. All trade disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin, and, where required for agricultural goods, phytosanitary certificates and food safety documentation. Payment to a related party or to a third-party commission agent is treated as high-risk and will require the same evidential standard as inbound capital. The salon should maintain separate NZD and a small multi-currency sweep account to allow natural hedging of USD and CNY exposures, with periodic conversion back to NZD under a board-approved treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts with a maximum tenor of 12 months and a board-approved limit of 120% of forecast trade exposures
Plain-vanilla NZD/CNY deliverable forward contracts for tea and ceramic import settlement where an underlying supply agreement exists
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only for converting a shareholder loan or long-term intercompany debt from foreign currency into NZD, subject to a documented non-derivative hedging purpose
Currency options (European style) with a premium paid upfront and no leverage, used solely to cap adverse NZD depreciation for future import payments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing only currencies of the tea origin market are permissible where local regulations restrict deliverable settlement, but must be transacted through the NZ tier-1 bank and settled in NZD or USD without any unregulated offshore counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of the company's incorporation date; filing window opens one month prior to the anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 200 (approximately USD 120) if not filed within 40 working days after the anniversary; continued non-compliance may result in the Registrar issuing a notice demanding payment and the company being referred for removal (administrative strike-off) from the Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Corporate Registers (via Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of the incorporation date, as part of the Annual Return filing obligation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same as Annual Return; false or misleading confirmation may trigger criminal penalties under the Companies Act 1993, and continued default may lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tax Return and Income Tax Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Terminal tax and return filing generally due by 7 April after the end of the 31 March balance date, or at the extended applicable date following the financial year; provisional taxpayers may file under the 2024/2025 filing date rules as determined by the IRD.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, late payment penalties (initial 1%) and interest charges on unpaid income tax; the tax assessment remains debt due and IRD may use collection and distress remedies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Schedule or Employer Monthly Schedule (EMS) and IRD Compliance (if any employees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly: employer schedules must be provided to IRD within 20 days following the end of each pay period month; annual declarations of payroll and RWT may be required by 31 May following the year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to NZD 250 per outstanding schedule, plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest; continued non-filing can lead to IRD enforcement actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month and six weeks after the end of each GST return period (GST returns can be filed one, two, or six-monthly; standard taxable period for most businesses is the two-month period, with the return due on the 28th day of the month following the end of the taxable period).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of NZD 50 (up to NZD 250) and late payment penalties; interest imposed on unpaid GST; failure to pay may result in IRD debt collection action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Franchise / Food and Beverage Business Annual Declaration (if applicable under local council regulations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Territorial Authority / City Council (where the tea salon operates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the date required by the local council's business licence or food safety registration conditions (typically 31 May or 31 March depending on council).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Renewal failure may restrict continued operation and may lead to suspension or cancellation of the food safety registration, and court fines of up to NZD 500,000 for operators under the Food Act 2014 for unregistered operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An audit is required for companies that are large (total assets or turnover exceeding NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalents) under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A specialty tea salon lounge with low-risk retail operations will generally be a small or medium entity and will not be subject to a statutory audit unless it is a subsidiary of a large company or the shareholders have elected an audit under the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 and 2; Tier 3 (overseas registration) and Tier 4 (non-large) entities may apply NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime or the New Zealand Accounting Standards Framework - Simple Format Reporting (for small and medium-sized entities). Non-reporting entities may use the NZ statutory preparation rules under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 1993, each company must maintain an accurate register of its directors, shareholders, and any ultimate shareholders where a nominee holds shares on trust. The Annual Return to the Companies Office requires the company to confirm the registered details (shareholding, director identities, and address for service). New Zealand does not require a separate annual UBO declaration; the shareholding and director information is confirmed annually. For the relevant interest, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) disclosure is not mandatory for local private companies unless there is a compliance trigger under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 for the reporting entity. Where the tea salon holds a compliant AML/CFT reporting position, it must undertake routine customer due diligence; however, the company, as a non-reporting entity for AML/CFT, is not subject to annual UBO filings.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: NZD 200 to NZD 500 (approximately USD 120 to USD 300) per annum for a registered agent or registered office service, if not maintained by the director directly.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For an exempt small specialty tea salon not requiring a statutory audit, if shareholders voluntarily require an audit, the market fee for a small hospitality entity may range from USD 3,000 to USD 8,000; a full licensed statutory audit, if applicable, would typically be USD 8,000 to USD 15,000 depending on size and complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential deduction available as an R&D Tax Credit equal to 15% of eligible expenditure where applicable. Loss carry-forward is unlimited in New Zealand subject to shareholder continuity (49%) and business continuity rules; encoded as 999 in the machine-readable schema to denote indefinite carry-forward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the Inland Revenue (IRD) myIR portal or using IRD-approved accounting and efiling software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following year-end. Terminal tax is due by 7 April following year-end. Tax agents may obtain extensions of time to file until 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 Section 1 – Business and Other Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from tea salon operations, lounge service charges, loose-leaf tea retail sales, ceramic merchandise, and any other assessable business income derived in New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with no fixed establishment or permanent establishment in New Zealand are normally not required to file an IR4. If a PE exists, include only income sourced in New Zealand and attributable to that PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions directly related to earning assessable income: raw tea purchases, rent, wages, depreciation, utilities, packaging, marketing, licensing and other ordinary business costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers may claim deductions only to the extent expenses are incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced income and are not otherwise disallowed by the applicable double tax agreement or domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable income after subtracting allowable deductions from gross assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, this line must reflect only New Zealand taxable income. Transfer pricing adjustments must be made before arriving at this figure where cross-border related-party transactions exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable on net taxable income calculated at the 28% corporate rate, subject to imputation credits, resident withholding tax credits, and any other available tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies should not reduce this amount for foreign tax credits unless a relevant treaty provision or domestic foreign tax credit rule clearly applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IR4 Section 5 – Tax Credits and Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid, RWT paid on interest/dividends, foreign dividend credits, imputation credits attached to dividends received, and any other credits are reported here to determine final refund or balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claiming treaty-reduced withholding rates must have lodged an IR372 non-resident withholding tax exemption certificate or supplied a valid tax residence certificate before payments were made.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for the first month or part thereof, with NZ$250 per month or part month thereafter. Late payment penalties accrue as an initial 1%, an additional 4% if unpaid after seven days, and 1% per month on the outstanding amount. Use-of-money interest is additionally imposed on all overdue and unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must provide the New Zealand payer with a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the relevant foreign tax authority. Prior to payment, the recipient should also register with IRD and apply for a certificate of exemption or file IR372 to substantiate the reduced NRWT rate. IRD may require evidence of beneficial ownership and economic substance before granting treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic NRWT rates are 15% on interest and 15% on royalties paid to non-residents. Under most NZ DTAs, interest is commonly reduced to 10% and royalties commonly to 10% or 5%, depending on beneficial ownership and intellectual property type. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may substitute for NRWT on qualifying interest where the payer is an approved issuer and conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$100 million group-wide revenue threshold; cross-border related-party goods/services transactions exceeding NZ$10 million, or cross-border related-party financing transactions exceeding NZ$5 million, trigger the requirement to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation including a Master File and Local File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to offshore financial centres. However, the IRD applies general anti-avoidance rules under the Income Tax Act 2007, requires substantive economic activity for tax residence and permanent establishment analysis, and insists that treaty benefits are available only to beneficial owners with genuine business substance. A shell company holding assets or receiving passive income without staff, premises, or business activity in New Zealand will be vulnerable to anti-avoidance reconstruction and treaty denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting tea lounge cash sales, omitting loose-leaf tea e-commerce revenue, inflating purchases from related parties, destroying accounting records, or filing a false IR4.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty equal to 150% of the evaded tax, plus use-of-money interest. Criminal conviction under Section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 can result in a fine of up to NZ$250,000 and imprisonment for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly participate in tax evasion face personal criminal liability, disqualification from managing companies, and orders for reparation or restitution. The corporate veil may be pierced where business is carried on reckantly under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the specialty tea salon through an opaque New Zealand shell company with no economic substance for the purpose of manufacturing treaty residence, misusing imputation credits, or diverting profits through artificial intra-group loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may invoke the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG1 and s GA1 of the Income Tax Act 2007), disregard the offending arrangement, reconstruct taxable income, and impose a 100% shortfall penalty for abusive tax avoidance, plus an additional 20% for taking an unacceptable tax position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly enter into or promote an abusive tax arrangement can be held personally liable for the resulting tax shortfall and penalties. Courts may order civil restitution and impose travel bans pending tax fraud or money laundering investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation after exceeding the NZ$100 million group revenue and NZ$10 million related-party goods/services or NZ$5 million financing thresholds, or pricing international purchases of premium tea stock and royalty payments to foreign affiliates without arm's length comparability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may adjust profits to the arm's length standard, deny deductions, and impose shortfall penalties of 40% for an unacceptable tax position or 100% for abusive tax avoidance, plus interest. Certain penalties may be reduced if contemporaneous documentation is supplied on request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer pricing statements known to be false or who cause the company to be used as an instrument of profit shifting can face personal civil penalties and, in egregious cases, criminal prosecution for evasion of tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the corporate entity as a facade with nominee shareholders, undisclosed beneficial owners, no local board decision-making, and no real commercial activity; or adding money-changing, remittance, or stored-value services without the required Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 compliance programme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML/CTF breaches can result in fines up to NZ$2 million per entity and civil penalty orders. IRD may disregard the shell arrangement for tax purposes, deny treaty benefits, and impose shortfall penalties. Money laundering offences may lead to imprisonment for up to seven years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted under AML/CTF legislation if they knowingly permit suspicious transactions without reporting. Freezing orders, travel bans, extradition, and disqualification from holding directorships are available where the company is used as a vehicle for financial crime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeatedly failing to file the IR4, ignoring IRD compliance notices, continuing to pay dividends while tax liabilities are unpaid, or charging GST without filing GST returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may issue default assessments under section 107B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, impose late filing penalties, late payment penalties, and use-of-money interest, and register a charge over company assets. Persistent non-filing can lead to strike-off and deregistration of the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be made personally liable for unpaid GST and PAYE withheld from employees if they allowed the company to trade while unable to meet those obligations. Illegal trading provisions under the Companies Act 1993 expose directors to personal liability and disqualification.
